text:
elaine: hi — installing our app from GitHub and can't import the client, hitting ImportError

elaine: example error when i run the app: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app/main.py", line 3, in <module>
    from redwood import RedwoodClient
ImportError: cannot import name 'RedwoodClient' from 'redwood' (unknown location)
```

sam: ugh, ok. did you pip install from pypi or from the repo? what does `pip freeze` show? python version? venv?

elaine: pip install was `pip install git+https://github.com/example-company/myservice.git@feature/redwood` (we vendor the SDK in a requirements file). python 3.10 in a venv. pip freeze below:
```
redwood==1.4.0
redwood-client==0.0.3
redwood-analytics==0.2.1
requests==2.31.0
other-lib==2.0.0
```

elaine: also tried `pip install redwood-inference` and it says already satisfied.

sarah: ah that pip freeze is suspicious — there's a package called `redwood` and another `redwood-client`. Can you run `pip show redwood` and `pip show redwood-inference`?

elaine: `pip show redwood` gives:
```
Name: redwood
Version: 0.1.2
Summary: Redwood analytics shim
Location: /home/elaine/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages
Requires: 
```
and `pip show redwood-inference` gives:
```
Name: redwood-inference
Version: 1.4.0
Location: /home/elaine/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood_inference-1.4.0-py3.10.egg
Requires: requests
```

sam: there we go — you have an unrelated package named `redwood` (note: top-level module name conflict). When you do `from redwood import RedwoodClient` python resolves to the other package's top-level module instead of the SDK. That explains the import error.

elaine: ohhh, makes sense. how did `redwood` get installed? it's a transitive dep of `redwood-analytics` in our requirements. is the SDK supposed to expose `redwood` as the top-level module?

sarah: our package on PyPI is `redwood-inference` and the SDK top-level package is `redwood_inference` (underscore) — older repos sometimes published under a different top-level name, and some internal packages use `redwood` too. Two options:
- change your imports to `from redwood_inference import Client` (if you want to use the canonical PyPI package), or
- uninstall the conflicting `redwood` package and re-install the SDK so `redwood` resolves to the SDK (not recommended if you need analytics).

sam: for a quick repro/verify, run these in your venv:
```bash
pip uninstall -y redwood redwood-client redwood-analytics
pip install redwood-inference==1.4.0
python -c "import pkgutil; print([m.name for m in pkgutil.iter_modules() if 'redwood' in m.name])"
python -c "from redwood_inference import Client; print('import ok')"
```

elaine: doing that now. one sec.

deploy-bot: deploy/ci: build passed for branch feature/redwood (job #342) :white_check_mark:

elaine: uninstall+reinstall worked. `from redwood_inference import Client` imports fine and app starts. but we have analytics dependency — can't remove it entirely.

sarah: two safe long-term fixes:
1) change your code to import the explicit top-level SDK package name `redwood_inference` (less surprising and won't conflict).
2) if you must use `from redwood import ...`, vendor/namespace the analytics package or ask analytics team to publish under a different name — but that's more invasive.

sam: also, when pip installing from GitHub make sure the egg/name matches the intended distribution name. If you do `pip install git+https://...#egg=redwood` pip will claim the package is named `redwood` which can mask the published PyPI package. Use `#egg=redwood-inference` or better point to the package root and let setup.cfg/pyproject define the name.

elaine: noted. i had `#egg=redwood` in our requirements.txt — that explains why git install created the wrong top-level package earlier. changed to `#egg=redwood-inference` and repinned.

sarah: nice. tl;dr for docs: add a quick note to the support KB about name collisions (redwood vs redwood_inference) + check for `pip show` and `pip freeze` as first troubleshooting steps.

elaine: thanks both — saved my morning :relieved:  

sam: amazing, marking resolved — please reopen if anything else crops up. :thumbsup:
